runs.title: Discount above limit: Thar Distributors Rawalpindi, 30% on SKU-103

assessment.explanation: Sales order SO-001-0056 applied a 30% discount (net price PKR 3,360 vs list PKR 4,800) on 1,292 cartons, with no trade‑promotion scheme reference (scheme_ref is null). The discount exceeds the 10% threshold, resulting in an amount at risk of PKR 1,240,320, which triggers a High severity breach.
assessment.root_cause: Discount approval process is not enforced at order entry.
assessment.recommended_action: Enforce that any discount greater than 10% must be linked to an approved trade‑promotion scheme before order release, and add system validation to require a scheme reference.

runs.title: Freight km above standard: Chenab Logistics (Pvt) Ltd, LHR-Faisalabad

assessment.explanation: Freight bill TRP-001-0036 billed 226 km versus the standard route distance of 185 km (RT-05), exceeding the 15% threshold by 22.2% and creating an excess amount of PKR 11,070. No diversion_note is provided, so there is no documented route diversion approved by the logistics desk.
assessment.root_cause: Missing documented diversion approval for the over‑billed route.
assessment.recommended_action: Require a documented diversion approval note for any freight bill that exceeds the standard route distance, and enforce system validation to block payment without such approval.

runs.title: Wage below minimum: E-10209 (HTR), PKR 33,500

assessment.explanation: The payslip PSL-001-0073 shows a gross pay of PKR 33,500 for July 2026 for contract worker Asad Malik (employee E-10209) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, while the provincial minimum wage is PKR 40,000, resulting in a shortfall of PKR 6,500. The employee is a full‑time contract worker with 48 contracted hours per week, so the pro‑rata exception does not apply.
assessment.root_cause: Payroll system failed to enforce the minimum wage rule for contract workers.
assessment.recommended_action: Update the payroll process to enforce the provincial minimum wage for all workers, including contract staff, and add a pre‑run validation to flag any wages below the minimum.

runs.title: Payment after termination: E-10311, PKR 867,817

assessment.explanation: The PKR 867,817 payment on 2026-07-12 (PSL-001-0074) is recorded as a "Full and final settlement: leave encashment and gratuity" for employee E-10311, who was terminated on 2026-06-11, matching the accepted legitimate explanation for post‑termination payments.
assessment.root_cause: The rule flagged a legitimate final settlement because it does not differentiate settlement payments from regular salary.
assessment.recommended_action: Ensure that all final settlement payments are clearly documented with remarks and linked to the employee's termination record to avoid future false alerts.

runs.title: Excessive hours: E-10275 (HTR), 69 h

assessment.explanation: Attendance record ATT-001-0091 shows 69 total hours, but a duplicate IN punch on 2026-07-11 (device HTR-03) was identified and corrected to 48.0 hours per timekeeping ticket TK-2170, which is within the 60‑hour weekly limit.
assessment.root_cause: Biometric device sync error causing a duplicate punch entry.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement a routine review of biometric sync errors and ensure duplicate punch corrections are documented and reflected in attendance calculations.

runs.title: Leaver with active ERP account: IABBASI2

assessment.explanation: The ERP user account U-4043 (IABBASI2) remains active and logged in on 2026-07-10, while the linked employee E-10083 was terminated on 2026-04-15. No inter-company transfer or re‑hire documentation exists, confirming a violation of the control that accounts must be locked on termination.
assessment.root_cause: Manual deprovisioning of the ERP account was not performed after the employee's resignation.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement an automated workflow to lock ERP accounts on the employee termination date and conduct a review of all active accounts for terminated staff.

runs.title: Leaver with active ERP account: ZBUTT1

assessment.explanation: User access record UAR-001-0027 shows that account U-4092 (ZBUTT1) remains Active even though the linked employee E-10162 was terminated on 2026-04-19, and the last login occurred on 2026-04-08 (before termination). The account was not locked on the termination date, violating control ITA-02 which requires immediate lockout of leaver accounts. No legitimate inter‑company transfer explanation is provided.
assessment.root_cause: Failure to execute the HR‑IT handover step to lock the ERP account on termination.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement an automated workflow that deactivates ERP user accounts on the employee's termination date and verify the lockout as part of the HR off‑boarding checklist.

runs.title: Self-approved journal: PKR 150,000

assessment.explanation: Journal JE-001-0039 for PKR 150,000 was posted and approved by the same user (YQURESHI5). The source is Manual, not a system-generated recurring entry, so the control requiring independent approval was not met.
assessment.root_cause: The approval workflow does not prevent the poster from also being the approver.
assessment.recommended_action: Configure the ERP to enforce that manual journals must be approved by a different user and add a validation rule to block self‑approval.

runs.title: Possible duplicate invoice: Saffron Manpower Services (Pvt) Ltd, PKR 700,719

assessment.explanation: Invoices APV-002-0041 (gross PKR 700,719, service period Jun 2026) and APV-002-0042 (gross PKR 700,719, service period Jul 2026) are from the same vendor for labour contractor services and cover different monthly service periods, matching the accepted legitimate explanation for recurring fixed‑fee services.
assessment.root_cause: The duplicate‑invoice rule does not consider service period, causing it to flag legitimate recurring invoices.
assessment.recommended_action: Document recurring labour contractor contracts and ensure invoice references clearly indicate the service period to prevent similar false‑positive alerts.

runs.title: Three-way match failure: Bolan Edible Oils (Pvt) Ltd, PKR 1,349,515 over-billed

assessment.explanation: Invoice APV-002-0043 (1108 bags at PKR 6,583 each) was posted and paid in full (payment PMT-002-0031) despite the goods receipt GRN-002-0037 confirming only 903 bags received. The over‑billed quantity of 205 bags results in an excess amount of PKR 1,349,515, breaching the three‑way match control.
assessment.root_cause: ERP variance check not enforced, allowing payment of mismatched invoices.
assessment.recommended_action: Configure the ERP to automatically block payments when invoice quantity exceeds the GRN quantity and require a manual variance approval before release.

runs.title: Payment soon after bank change: Hingol Agro Mills (Pvt) Ltd, PKR 197,908

assessment.explanation: The bank account change for vendor V-1017 was verified by a call-back to the registered contact on 2026-07-14 (BCR-002-0001) before any payments were made. Subsequent payments on 2026-07-16 (PMT-002-0032) and 2026-07-19 (PMT-002-0009) therefore complied with the control's verification requirement.
assessment.root_cause: Proper verification process was followed for the vendor bank change.
assessment.recommended_action: Ensure that the call-back verification documentation is consistently attached to the payment records and retained in the audit trail for future reviews.

runs.title: Credit limit exceeded: Mehran Distributors Hyderabad, PKR 1,961,086 over

assessment.explanation: Sales order SO-002-0056 (order value PKR 3,045,600) was released while the customer's total exposure (outstanding PKR 12,815,486 + order PKR 3,045,600 = PKR 15,861,086) exceeded its approved credit limit of PKR 13,900,000, resulting in an amount at risk of PKR 1,961,086. The release note is null and no CFO‑approved credit extension is documented, violating control O2C-01.
assessment.root_cause: Failure to enforce the credit‑limit override approval process.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement a mandatory CFO approval step for any sales order that would exceed a distributor's credit limit and ensure the approval is recorded in the release note before order release.

runs.title: Credit limit exceeded: Mehran Distributors Sukkur, PKR 280,550 over

assessment.explanation: Sales order SO-002-0057 was released despite the combined exposure (PKR 2,480,550) exceeding the distributor's credit limit (PKR 2,200,000) by PKR 280,550. No release note or CFO-approved credit extension is documented (release_note is null), violating the O2C-01 control.
assessment.root_cause: The credit limit override approval process was not enforced for this order.
assessment.recommended_action: Require a documented CFO credit extension approval before releasing any sales order that would exceed a customer's credit limit, and enforce a system block until such approval is attached.

runs.title: Credit limit exceeded: Kirthar Distributors Gujranwala, PKR 101,564 over

assessment.explanation: Sales order SO-002-0058 exceeded the distributor's credit limit by PKR 101,564, but the release note records a temporary credit extension approved by the CFO (ref CE-2026-082) valid through 2026-07-19, which meets the control's accepted legitimate explanation.
assessment.root_cause: The rule flagged the order without considering the documented CFO-approved credit extension.
assessment.recommended_action: Store CFO credit extension approvals in a central repository and ensure they are linked to the related sales orders for audit traceability.

runs.title: Discount above limit: Crescent Distributors Faisalabad, 28% on SKU-104

assessment.explanation: Sales order SO-002-0059 applied a 28% discount (net price PKR 1,296 vs list PKR 1,800) on 1,065 cartons, resulting in a discount beyond the allowed 10% of PKR 345,060. The order contains no scheme reference or note indicating an approved trade-promotion scheme, which is required for discounts above 10%. Therefore the control was not satisfied.
assessment.root_cause: The discount approval process was not enforced at order release, allowing unauthorised discounts.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement a mandatory validation step that prevents order release unless a valid trade-promotion scheme reference is attached for discounts exceeding 10%. Train order entry staff on the requirement.

runs.title: Freight km above standard: Shalimar Logistics (Pvt) Ltd, LHR-Faisalabad

assessment.explanation: Freight bill TRP-002-0036 billed 684 km (PKR 184,680) against the standard route distance of 555 km (RT-05) – a 23.2% excess – and the diversion_note field is null, providing no approved justification for the over‑billing.
assessment.root_cause: Lack of documented route diversion approval.
assessment.recommended_action: Require the logistics desk to obtain and attach a documented diversion approval for any route deviation before processing freight payments.

runs.title: Freight km above standard: Thar Goods Transport (Pvt) Ltd, KHI-Sukkur

assessment.explanation: Freight bill TRP-002-0037 shows billed kilometres of 579 versus the standard 475 (21.9% excess) but includes a diversion note stating the route was diverted due to a motorway closure (NHA advisory) and that the diversion was approved by the logistics desk on 2026-07-16, which matches the accepted legitimate explanation.
assessment.root_cause: Manual verification of diversions is not integrated into the automated freight billing check.
assessment.recommended_action: Ensure all approved diversions are recorded in the logistics system and attached to freight bills for audit verification.

runs.title: Wage below minimum: E-10039 (LHR), PKR 29,800

assessment.explanation: The employee Salman Butt (E-10039) is a contract worker with 30 contracted hours per week (see employee record E-10039). The pro‑rated minimum wage for Punjab is 40,000 × 30/48 = 25,000 PKR, and the payslip PSL-002-0070 shows a gross pay of 29,800 PKR for July 2026, which exceeds the pro‑rated minimum, so the exception is a false positive.
assessment.root_cause: Payroll control did not account for contracted hours in the minimum‑wage check.
assessment.recommended_action: Update payroll validation rules to automatically apply the pro‑rated minimum‑wage calculation for part‑time and contract workers.

runs.title: Payment after termination: E-10154, PKR 46,000

assessment.explanation: Payslip PSL-002-0071 shows a regular salary payment of PKR 46,000 on 2026-07-19 to employee E-10154, whose HR record (E-10154) confirms termination on 2026-06-01. The payment is classified as "Regular salary" rather than a final settlement, violating the PAY-02 control that only final settlements may be paid after termination.
assessment.root_cause: Payroll processing failed to differentiate regular salary from final settlement for a terminated employee.
assessment.recommended_action: Update the payroll system to block regular salary payments for terminated employees and require explicit classification and approval for any post‑termination settlement.

runs.title: Excessive hours: E-10001 (KHI), 63 h

assessment.explanation: Attendance record ATT-002-0091 shows a duplicate IN punch on 2026-07-18 due to a device sync error; the timekeeping ticket TK-3624 corrected the weekly hours to 54, which is within the 60‑hour limit.
assessment.root_cause: Biometric device sync error caused a duplicate punch.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement routine checks for biometric device sync errors and ensure any duplicate punches are corrected and documented promptly.

runs.title: Leaver with active ERP account: MRANA8

assessment.explanation: Employee E-10123 (Maryam Rana) was terminated on 2026-06-20 due to an inter-company transfer and re‑hired under a new ID (E-10322) on the same date, which matches the control's accepted legitimate explanation. Therefore the active ERP account (U-4069) is a permissible exception.
assessment.root_cause: Process gap in deactivating legacy accounts during inter-company transfers.
assessment.recommended_action: Update the termination workflow to automatically lock the legacy ERP account when an inter-company transfer is recorded.

runs.title: Self-approved journal: PKR 2,570,000

assessment.explanation: Journal JE-002-0039 for PKR 2,570,000 was posted on 2026-07-15 by Zeeshan Lodhi (ZLODHI5) and approved by the same user, with source marked as Manual. This violates the GL-01 control which requires an independent approver for manual journals, especially those above PKR 1,000,000.
assessment.root_cause: Insufficient segregation of duties in the journal posting process.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement system controls to prevent same-user approval of manual journals and enforce independent review for all manual entries above PKR 1,000,000.

runs.title: Self-approved journal: PKR 110,000

assessment.explanation: Journal JE-002-0040 (PKR 110,000) was posted on 2026-07-16 as a manual entry and was both posted and approved by SJAMALI1 (Shazia Jamali), violating the control that requires an independent approver for manual journals.
assessment.root_cause: The approval workflow does not enforce segregation of duties for manual journal postings.
assessment.recommended_action: Implement system controls to prevent a user from approving their own manual journal entries and enforce independent review for all manual journals.
